note: Applications that NAME a Secret nothing in the dev bootstrap roster mints.
An entry here is a claim that the missing Secret is ACCEPTABLE, and the only
acceptable reasons are structural: the Application never runs a pod in this
lane, or the credential is metal-only and the Application is excluded here.
'Someone will add it later' is not one of them -- that is the state this
audit exists to make loud, and it was reached once already (redis).
Every entry needs a `reason` and a `liftsWhen`. An entry that stops matching
fails as STALE, which is how a lifted exclusion forces the question again.

entries.reason: STRUCTURAL: temporal is in DEV_EXCLUDED_REASONS, so the dev lane never applies this Application at all and no cluster in this lane ever resolves the name. The credential is metal-only, alongside the external datastore it authenticates to -- the same store the pending 0.59.0 -> 1.6.0 migration has to rewrite from `server.config.persistence.default` to `.datastores.<name>`.
entries.liftsWhen: temporal leaves DEV_EXCLUDED_REASONS. This entry then names a Secret an applied Application needs, and the fix is the roster, not this file.

entries.reason: STRUCTURAL, and the same reason as `temporal-default-store` above: temporal is dev-excluded, so nothing in this lane resolves the name. Listed SEPARATELY rather than folded into one entry because they are two distinct Secrets for two distinct datastores (default and visibility), and an acknowledgement that covered both under one key would keep applying if only one of them were ever created.
entries.liftsWhen: temporal leaves DEV_EXCLUDED_REASONS, exactly as for the default store.

entries.reason: OPTIONAL CACHE, not a hard dependency: server.volumes.secret.optional is true, so a missing Secret does not Pending the pod. The sidecar (src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/openbao-unseal-sidecar.ts) returns [] on an empty mount and stays up. Shares are produced by the gated init ceremony, not by DEV_BOOTSTRAP_SECRETS -- minting Shamir material into the CI roster would put unseal keys in etcd, which is refused. Init stays gated; this name is the kind/CI Shamir cache path.
entries.liftsWhen: A producer writes openbao-unseal-shares after the gated init (USB / Keychain / host projector), or metal seal pkcs11 replaces this sidecar and the volume is removed.

entries.reason: 081M1...WP3 (crd-provider-consumer-order.ts / audit-existing-secret-is-minted.ts's new raw-manifest scan). controller.yaml and portal.yaml both declare `imagePullSecrets: [{name: ghcr-pull}]` on a real pod spec -- caught only by the new collectRawSecretReferences() scan, since the existing valuesObject scan never looks at plain workload manifests. MINTED FOR CI/DEV ONLY: DEV_GHCR_PULL_SECRET (dev-cluster/lib.ts) mints `ghcr-pull` per dev/CI cluster at bring-up, and argocd-health-test.ts's assertDevRegistryPullSecretPresent refuses an included run without it -- but that is a runtime harness action that never touches a real cluster. NOTHING IN THE COMMITTED TREE MINTS IT: no SealedSecret, no ExternalSecret, no Secret manifest for `ghcr-pull` exists anywhere under full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications. This is why `platform` is ALSO in DEV_EXCLUDED_REASONS (argocd-health-test.ts) with a long entry ending 'WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED ... no job has presented that token to GHCR and been served a layer' -- the same gap, found independently by two different mechanisms. On metal, without this Secret, both platform pods ImagePullBackOff forever, and since resource.customizations.health.argoproj.io_Application now makes ArgoCD wave-gating wait for platform (wave -20) to be Healthy before wave -10 and everything after it starts, this is the SINGLE MOST SEVERE stall risk this analysis found: an unfixed metal install would deadlock at wave -20, before nearly the entire cluster.
entries.liftsWhen: A SealedSecret or ExternalSecret for `ghcr-pull` in namespace `zeta-platform` is committed to full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/platform/ (the same shape DEV_FORGEJO_ADMIN_SECRET or the ziti admin credential use), sourced from a real GHCR PAT/deploy-token the maintainer provisions -- a credential-provisioning decision, not a mechanical fix this audit can make on its own. Tracked as workitem 081M33TN49G087G0R000X5ZJ75 (make the GHCR packages public, or project the credential via full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/zeta-creds-to-k8s.nix + the INJECTION-POINTS.md rail).

entries.reason: 081M1...WP3 raw-manifest scan finding, and ALREADY SELF-DOCUMENTED in the tree before this audit existed: orleans/statefulset.yaml:8-10 reads 'Replicas stay at 0 ... the redis-auth secret this pod projects does not exist in the tree yet -- the redis Application says create via Sealed Secret / Vault. Bump to >= 1 once that secret is provisioned.' The reference itself is OPTIONAL (statefulset.yaml:61 -- `secretKeyRef: { name: redis-auth, key: password, optional: true }`), so a missing Secret does not Pending the pod -- same shape as the openbao-unseal-shares entry above. And StatefulSet.spec.replicas is 0, so no pod is even scheduled today: this is a dormant reference, not a live blocker. redis's OWN Application.yaml has the identical unminted reference via valuesObject (auth.existingSecret: redis-auth), which the OTHER scan already reports as minted-by-dev-roster-only -- the raw scan surfaces the same metal gap a second time, from orleans's side.
entries.liftsWhen: A SealedSecret or ExternalSecret for `redis-auth` is committed (redis/Application.yaml's own comment names the intended mechanism), at which point orleans's replicas can also move off 0.

entries.reason: 081M1...WP3 raw-manifest scan finding. kubevirt-operator.yaml:8592-8617 projects `kubevirt-operator-certs` as a volume on the operator Deployment -- but the SAME vendored manifest grants the operator's ClusterRole/Role `secrets` verbs including a rule scoped to the literal resourceName `kubevirt-operator-certs` (line 6976). This is the standard operator self-signed-webhook-cert pattern: virt-operator CREATES this Secret itself at startup (the same runtime-registration shape as its CRDs -- see DECLARED_OPERATOR_CRDS in crd-provider-consumer-order.ts for kubevirt.io/VirtualMachine, which is the identical class of 'invisible to a static manifest scan, provided by the running controller'). Nothing needs to mint it in git.
entries.liftsWhen: Never, structurally -- this is the correct steady state for a self-managing operator credential, not a gap awaiting a fix. Recorded here rather than added to BUILTIN-style exemption logic because it is a single named Secret, not a class of kind/group this audit already models.
